_note: Written by the scheduled web & social sweep (and by hand). Every item needs a sourceUrl that was opened and checked. kinds: event (needs title+start+url, or just a Luma url), program (application windows), news (recaps, announcements), override (corrects a crawled event by id).

items.title: Make Something Agents Want
items.note: Two-day hackathon at YC's SF office on building for agents as the user: agent experience, headless MCPs, docs written for agents. 225 spots.

items.title: TreeHacks 2027
items.note: Stanford's flagship 36-hour hackathon. Open to enrolled undergrad and grad students worldwide; Stanford students are not auto-accepted.
Applications were due Sept 13 (priority) and Sept 20 (regular) at hive.hackberkeley.org.

items.name: Y Combinator — Winter 2027 batch
items.note: On-time deadline Nov 2 at 8pm PT; decisions by Dec 11. Batch runs January–March in San Francisco. Late applications are still reviewed.

items.name: a16z speedrun
items.note: Applications accepted on a rolling basis. Up to $1M first check, targeting a two-week close.

items.name: Berkeley SkyDeck — Batch 24
items.note: Applications for Batch 24 open in January. Batch 23 starts Nov 2, 2026.

items.name: TreeHacks 2027 hacker applications
items.note: Event Feb 12–14, 2027 at Stanford. Travel, meals and lodging covered for accepted hackers.

items.title: YC wrapped “Make Something Agents Want”, a two-day hackathon on building for AI agents
items.body: 225 builders at YC's SF office worked on agent experience: headless MCP servers, agent-readable docs and token-efficient APIs.

items.title: YC Winter 2027 applications close Nov 2
items.body: On-time applicants hear back by Dec 11. Spring, Summer and Fall 2027 early-decision applications are open too.

items.title: TreeHacks 2027 is taking applications for Feb 12–14 at Stanford
items.body: Open to college students worldwide. Travel, meals and lodging are covered for accepted hackers.

items.foundVia: Falcon Hacks site (via Hack Club Bay Area list)

items.name: South Park Commons Founder Fellowship — Spring 2027
items.note: Fall 2026 applications are closed. SPC says Spring 2027 applications open later this year; no date given.

items.name: Z Fellows
items.note: One-week program, mostly virtual, ending with an in-person day in San Francisco or New York. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline. Optional $10,000 investment at a $1B cap.

items.name: PearX — W27
items.note: Regular applications for W27 closed Oct 4; applications submitted after that are reviewed on a rolling basis. Pear has offices in San Francisco and Menlo Park.

items.title: Cerebral Valley and Crusoe ran The Recursive Agents Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: A one-day, in-person hackathon held during PyTorch Conference week, with $25,000 in cash and an NVIDIA RTX 5090 as prizes. Winners were not posted on the event page.

items.title: HackerSquad ran the ExecuTorch Hackathon at Founders, Inc. in San Francisco
items.body: A two-day on-device AI hackathon on Oct 17–18 with Qualcomm, Meta, GitHub and the PyTorch Foundation during Open Source AI Week. Top team per track received Meta AI glasses and an Arduino UNO Q; winners were not posted on the event page.

items.title: Granola and Anthropic ran a GTM & Marketing Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: An evening hackathon at Granola SF for non-technical GTM and marketing operators, who built with Claude and Granola context over MCP and demoed to judges. Winners were not posted on the event page.

items.name: Entrepreneur First — San Francisco residencies
items.note: EF says it accepts applications for its U.S. funding and fellowships and San Francisco residencies on a rolling basis. Its Bridge Residency in SF (Winter 2027, 8 weeks for young Europeans) starts February 2027.
